scope: November's sessions and a review of every 1.0.0.14 report: SteamVR's dashboard volume applied to the captured game audio (patch 0023); SteamVR's safe mode found before a session is stranded, and undone from the headset PC; a USB hub nested too deep (Bazzite), the headset's USB dropping out and controllers on but untracked, each named; the bitrate starting where the last session of the stream settled; the audio's aim no longer raised by stalls (patch 0022); a lower power draw than a smooth session's pointed out; the network settings check counting paused Wi-Fi adapters; an unplugged Wi-Fi adapter forgotten; the rendering PC's capture stalls recorded with the encoder's send time. Every package carries version 1.0.0.15.

from_the_sessions.what: 1.0.0.14 sessions in November on the reference setup, wired, and every 1.0.0.14 report the maintainer sent.
put_right: SteamVR's dashboard volume slider did nothing in the headset: the loopback capture is the device's mix before its volume
Start searched for the host until it gave up when SteamVR had blocked the driver after a crash (safe mode)
a session that ended in 'texture submission failed: 105' after the headset's USB dropped out, explained as nothing
controllers that were on but couldn't see the base stations, unexplained
the bitrate stepping down for the first minute of every session
game audio left late after a stall of the whole stream (the aim rose 10 ms per underrun, once to 125 ms)
the network settings check missing adapters paused by VROSTBridge, and a Wi-Fi adapter unplugged mid-session retried
from_the_sessions.not_put_right: what makes the rendering PC's network send stall (now recorded as capture_stalls), and USB depth on Windows

changes: patches/0023-host-game-audio-capture.patch: IAudioEndpointVolume on the captured device, read every 50 ms, its gain ramped across each packet before the limiter; VROST_AUDIO_CAPTURE volume_db
patches/0022-client-audio-playback.patch: the playback aim rises only for an underrun whose gap was within 30 ms of the aim

host/steamvr_driver.py (new), host/control.py, launcher/session_link.py (feature driver-unblock, /unblock), launcher/app.py, launcher/desktop.html, launcher/game_ui.py: safe mode read before a launch and from vrserver.txt after it, and undone from either PC while SteamVR is closed

launcher/headset_hardware.py (new), launcher/app.py: deep USB hubs from /sys/bus/usb/devices; HeadsetWatch over HEAD_TRACKING, CONTROLLER_STATE and INPUT lines for a USB dropout and untracked controllers
launcher/stream_budget.py, launcher/app.py: BitrateGovernor.settled() remembered per codec, size, refresh and network (bitrate_memory)
launcher/network_settings.py, launcher/wifi_others.py: paused adapters counted, a stale answer rechecked, an unplugged adapter forgotten
launcher/headset_audio.py: a Beyond accessory-port audio device whose name runs into the Beyond's
host/events.py: capture_stalls with the encoder's transmit_max_us
scripts/fetch_upstream.py: the applied patch set recorded in the checkout's git folder
scripts/Build-Host-Cross.py, scripts/Build-Client-Linux.sh: build folders mapped out of the driver and the Linux transport, and checked
scripts/Build-FFmpeg-Windows.sh: the version label FFmpeg's own (GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES) and no time stamp (SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0 for the stripping install), both checked

host.driver: rebuilt: ALVR f5023f8e with patches 0001 to 0023 (0023 changed), the build folders mapped out

bazzite_client.native_how: the transport rebuilt for patch 0022; the native client and runtime probe are 1.0.0.14's code with the new version label (the client's dynamic-link tables follow the new transport)
bazzite_client.frozen_companion: frozen again with PyInstaller 6.22.3 / Python 3.12.3; each module is the repository's source as Python 3.12 compiles it; the bundled zlib and liblzma are Ubuntu 24.04's current builds of the same versions (1.3, 5.4.5)

windows_client.native_how: the transport rebuilt for patch 0022; the native client and runtime probe are 1.0.0.14's code with the new version label (the import hints follow this machine's Windows SDK); FFmpeg's DLLs built again from the same source, identical to 1.0.0.9's build apart from the header time stamp and checksum, now zero

toolchain: Ubuntu 24.04, GCC 13.3.0, CMake 3.28.3 and Ninja (Linux client); Rust 1.97.1, clang-cl/lld-link/llvm-lib 19.1.1 and an xwin Windows SDK 10.0.26100 (driver, Windows transport, Windows client, launchers); libvpl 2.15.0 static (driver); mingw-w64 GCC (Windows FFmpeg); PyInstaller 6.22.3 / Python 3.12.3; NSIS 3.09; ReportLab with mermaid-cli (PDFs); Wine 9.0 with Mesa lavapipe; Node 22 (page checks).
